runs.name: Willis Lease Finance Corporation; Nasdaq WLFC, SEC CIK 0001018164, a lessor and servicer of commercial aircraft and aircraft engines in two segments, Leasing and Related Operations and Spare Parts Sales; three-for-one split 2026-07-17; WNG II portfolio bought 2026-08-24; Series B preferred to the Development Bank of Japan 2026-09-29; AerCap and FTAI the filing rivals the 10-K names, six non-filers flagged
runs.entry: Price **$37.61** (quote of 2026-10-16 printed by `tools/run.py`, aggregator, flagged), post-split basis. Shares **22,808 thousand** issued at 2026-06-30, unvested restricted stock included, the cover count 21,144,111 at 2026-07-31 beside it (10-Q for the quarter to 2026-06-30, accession 0001018164-26-000068; repurchased shares retired, no treasury stock; the difference is 1,663,635 unvested restricted shares; no common issued in the later 8-Ks); a three-for-one forward split effective 2026-07-17 (8-K 0001193125-26-307870), every per-share figure on the post-split basis; cap **$857.8M** ($795.2M on the cover count). Sovereign **5.43%** (US Treasury daily par yield curve, 30-year, 2026-10-15). Filings read: 10-K FY2025 (0001018164-26-000036) and its 10-K/A (0001018164-26-000041, Inline XBRL only); 10-Q Q2 2026; DEF 14A filed 2026-04-24 (0001193125-26-177136); 10-Ks FY2024, FY2023, FY2021, FY2020, FY2019 and FY2016; the 2026 8-Ks for the split, WNG II, the Series B preferred, the convertible notes and a building purchase. Cross-check: 2025 operating cash $283,235 thousand on the filed statement equals the tag, and four earlier years match. `tools/run.py`'s capex (property and furnishings only) set aside: it does not see the sale proceeds of leased equipment, so owner cash was recast by hand with fleet purchases, sale proceeds, gains, write-downs and the full tax provision. The brief departed in one stated place: six lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7, listed in the run file. **Q1 IN**: a spread-and-residual lessor of 363 engines and 20 aircraft to 69 lessees in 37 countries, Leasing $109.0M of 2025 segment operating income and Spare Parts a $4.4M loss, the model and the funding the same in every 10-K FY2016 to FY2025. **Q2 OUT**: engine leasing a commodity-type field on the filer's own account (operators 'utilize several leasing companies', engines bought by 'an auction bidding process', rivals that 'may have lower costs of capital' in every 10-K read) and WLFC not its low-cost operator: cost of debt 4.7% mean 2016 to 2025 against AerCap 4.0% (higher in nine years of ten, equal in 2020), FTAI 6.9%; pre-tax return on assets 5.8% against AerCap 5.1% and FTAI 5.2%, about a point over its own debt, below it in 2021 and 2022; overhead 4.2% of assets against AerCap 0.7%. Six named rivals do not file with the SEC or file only inside a parent (Shannon, Pratt & Whitney, Rolls-Royce Partners Finance, ELFC, MTU, SMBC); StandardAero files and was set aside as a repairer. Q3 to Q12 not reached. Facts after the stop: equity tripled to $709M from retained earnings, debt 3.3 to 4.8 times equity in every year read, substantially all assets pledged, no goodwill, cash tax near nil and a deferred tax liability of $264.8M; WNG II closed 2026-08-24 at an adjusted price of about $262.9M against the $379.3M base, ten engines and six aircraft to be placed in joint ventures or managed vehicles; Series B preferred of 1,750,000 shares at $20.00, 8.09%, to the Development Bank of Japan, closed 2026-09-29. **Integrity facts recorded, not judged** (DEF 14A): the Executive Chairman holds about 40% and was paid $52.09M in 2025, the CEO $19.21M, against net income to common of $108.1M; the bonus pool funded at about 255% of target on pre-tax income that included a $43.0M gain on selling BAML to the company's own 50% joint venture; Adjusted EBITDA featured; a 900,000-share option to the Chairman and shares bought from him directly. Owner cash, all-equity after maintenance: $111.6M a year over the 2020 to 2025 cycle, $132.9M over the literal 2021 to 2025 window; after interest and preferred dividends $37.2M and $53.8M. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: value **-$58.57 to -$18.47** a share (all-equity, cycle base; claims ahead of the common $2,476.6M, net debt at 2026-06-30 plus the WNG II price plus preferred at liquidation less the Series B cash) against $37.61, the literal window -$33.03 to -$1.28, equity-only $10.06 to $18.51; the best permitted case 3.35% at the price, no case earns the floor; fair **-$83.51 all-equity** ($2.81 equity-only); not armed, the box being OUT at Q2. A CONVENTION of the run: the full tax provision charged, cash tax beside. Contamination declared by the analyst: the opening commit subjects (HRI), the memory index lines, and one name-pattern test of `Test Runs/` file names for this company before the template copy, which returned nothing; none used. Commits 08af694c, 923b16f3 (Step 0, balance sheets and Q1), dd62a8fd (Q2), 6ccd2dc3 (close). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's `check_ids.py` 68 id citations, 51 distinct, 24 quoted fragments, PASS; the dispatcher's `dispatcher_check.py` 26 fragments, 24 matched, the 2 flagged being the filing's own words ('lower costs of capital') quoted before an id that heads the next clause, no slip, no missing id, no E-id. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **A slip in the dispatcher's brief, for the record**: the brief said the 10-K's Competition passage names the nine rivals; the analyst found them in Item 1A, the Competition passage of Item 1 naming none. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) no rule for a lessor's maintenance spending, the fleet being both plant and product (gains on sale, write-downs and sales-type principal treated by the analyst's choice, said so); (2) 'Whose tax' silent on a company that pays almost no cash tax because tax depreciation runs ahead; (3) specific (a)'s cycle base when the series begins after the prior trough; (4) redeemable preferred on the equity-only basis; (5) on the all-equity basis a spread business values negative in every case while equity-only is positive, so the basis can dominate the reporting figures for any leveraged lessor or lender. Could not get: AerCap's engine business apart from its aircraft; any SEC figures for the six non-filing rivals; a full prior cycle (data from 2015); whether the signed $118.0M building purchase has closed.
runs.narr: OUT at Q2 after Q1 IN (a spread-and-residual engine and aircraft lessor, 363 engines and 20 aircraft to 69 lessees). Engine leasing a commodity-type field on the filer's own account, customers using several lessors and engines bought at auction, and WLFC not its low-cost operator: cost of debt 4.7% mean 2016 to 2025 against AerCap 4.0% (higher in nine years of ten), overhead 4.2% of assets against 0.7%, pre-tax return on assets 5.8% against AerCap 5.1% and FTAI 5.2%, about a point over its own debt across the cycle. Facts after the stop: debt 3.3 to 4.8 times equity, assets pledged, WNG II bought 2026-08-24 for about $262.9M, Series B preferred to the Development Bank of Japan; integrity facts recorded, not judged: the Executive Chairman paid $52.09M in 2025 against net income to common of $108.1M, a bonus pool at about 255% of target on pre-tax income including a $43.0M gain on a sale to the company's own joint venture. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: value -$58.57 to -$18.47 all-equity against $37.61, no case earning the floor; fair -$83.51 all-equity, $2.81 equity-only, not armed. Framework gaps for the operator: a lessor's maintenance spending; tax when little cash tax is paid; the cycle base when data starts after the trough; redeemable preferred on the equity-only basis; the all-equity basis dominating any leveraged lessor.
